The list is not a frequency, POS, script, length or even semantic class - the corpus-frequency correlation is r = -0.03 and letter/suffix features stay at AUC ~0.5, ' vector' 1.185, ' sequence' 1.162, ' tensor' 0.756 and ' matrix' 0.575 fire while ' data', ' model', ' number', ' string', ' result', ' function', ' method' and ' system' are exactly 0.000 - it is an arbitrary fixed list with an academic-technical flavour (' CRISPR' 1.053, ' genotype' 1.015, ' codon' 0.974, ' genomic' 0.892, ' epitope' 0.866, ' transgene' 0.863; ' argc' 0.993, ' zip' 0.936, ' hash' 0.924, ' cache' 0.912, ' constexpr' 0.826; ' anymore' 1.222, ' cloned' 1.186, ' nationally' 1.000, ' supporters' 0.955; ' norm' 0.331, ' today' 0.357, ' word' 0.445, ' loading' 0.426 are also on it) plus a 3-7x enrichment for non-Latin-script byte pieces (Korean 20%, Greek 19%, Bengali 19%, Hindi 13% of pieces active vs 2.7% English; 343 of its top 500 pieces are non-ASCII), and the negative pole is the separate GELU dip, near its 0.170 maximum on another arbitrary set (' time', ' people', ' I', 'er', ' model' at -0.169 to -0.170) while the highest-frequency pieces are only slightly negative (' the' -0.022, ' of' -0.028).
